memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron and say to him, 'When you set up the lamps, see that all seven light up the area in front of the lampstand.'" Aaron did so; he set up the lamps so that they faced forward on the lampstand, just as the Lord commanded Moses. - Num 8:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives instructions about the lampstand in the tabernacle: the seven lamps were to be set so that their light shone forward, illuminating the area in front. In the holy place, where no natural sunlight reached, this lamp was the source of light. It was arranged deliberately so its glow would fall where it was needed.

There is something lovely in this small detail. The light was not meant to shine only for its own sake, glowing quietly in a corner. It was positioned to shine outward and forward, giving light to the space around it. Light exists to be shared.

This is a gentle picture of how our lives are meant to work. God does not give us His light so we can keep it hidden. He fills us with His truth, His love, and His presence so that the light might shine forward — onto the path in front of us and into the lives of those around us.

Jesus said plainly, "You are the light of the world," and He told us not to hide our light but to let it shine before others, so they may see and give glory to God (Matt 5:14-16). And He Himself is the true Light: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me... will have the light of life" (John 8:12).

Let the light God has placed in you shine forward today — lighting your own way, and warming the lives of others for His glory.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is the light God gave you shining forward, or hidden away?
- Who around you needs the light of God's love and truth?
- How can you let your light shine for God's glory today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the light You have placed in me through Christ. Help me not to hide it, but to let it shine forward for others and for Your glory. Amen.
